title: OCX index deployment policy
description: `.github/index-policy.json` — one index deployment's committed configuration. Not wire contract: the served URL shapes are frozen for every index alike, and this decides only what THIS index puts in them. `core/policy.py`'s parse_index_policy is the runtime authority; this file exists so an operator's editor can autocomplete and pre-flight the config. The two are held together by the shared fixture corpus in tests/fixtures/policy/.

$schema.description: Points at this file. Accepted and ignored by the parser.

name.description: Logical prefix every published root carries — `ocx.sh` for the public index, `acme.corp` for a corporate one. Also the registry key an ocx client configures as [registries."<name>"] index = "…", which is why it has exactly the registry-host grammar: no scheme, no port, no path, no trailing dot, lowercase. Required, with no default — an index that does not declare its own name would publish under another deployment's.

name_segments.description: How many `/`-separated segments follow `name` in a package id, and so how deep `p/**` nests. `2` gives `acme.corp/<namespace>/<package>`. Published in the rendered config.json because no client can derive it from a tree. The upper bound is not an opinion about hierarchy depth — it exists so every derived path length stays bounded. Required, with no default.

registry_hosts.description: G-03's allowlist: hosts whose `oci://` repositories this index will admit. Widening it is a supply-chain trust decision, which is why it lives in a reviewed file and never in a settings-page variable. Bare lowercase hosts only — a scheme, a port or a path would allowlist nothing, because the check compares against a URL's parsed hostname. A registry on a non-default port is still allowlisted by its bare host.

reserved_namespaces.description: First path segments this operator reserves — a brand, an internal prefix. The STRUCTURAL reservations (`p`, `o`, `c`, `config`, `schema`, …) are deliberately not expressible here: they follow from the served URL shapes and hold for every index, so the bot applies them unconditionally. Defaults to none.

governance.description: How the governance lane decides a merge. Defaults apply when the block is absent or empty.

auto_merge.description: `owners` — a machine-lane PR auto-merges when its author owns every touched root (the public index's policy). `never` — every PR waits for a human. `always` — any machine-lane PR auto-merges.

ci.description: What `indexbot ci` renders, and for which forge. Not how the bot picks a forge API at run time — that comes from the runner's own variables. Defaults apply when the block is absent or empty.

forge.description: `github` covers github.com and GitHub Enterprise; `gitlab` covers gitlab.com and any self-hosted GitLab, including CE.

owner.description: The repository owner / GitLab namespace, for the cron-upstream-only guard every scheduled job carries. `indexbot ci` refuses to render without it rather than guess: a fork inherits every schedule in a workflow file and would run it against its own stale copy. It renders inside a quoted expression scalar (`github.repository_owner == '<owner>'`, `$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE == "<owner>"`), so — unlike `run` and `setup` below — it takes the package-namespace grammar (letters, digits, single hyphens), composed with `/` for a GitLab subgroup path, rather than just a newline ban: a `'` or `"` would break out of that scalar.

run.description: The command a generated job uses to invoke the bot. REQUIRED for `indexbot ci`, with no default, and it must not resolve the version at job start. It is what the privileged governance job runs — on GitHub, a job holding `contents: write` under `pull_request_target`, whose token can move an unprotected base branch and squash-merge a pull request — so `uvx ocx-indexbot`, which fetches the latest release when the step starts, is refused rather than defaulted to. Pin by lockfile (`uv run --project bot-tools --frozen -- indexbot`; without `--frozen` or `--locked`, `uv run` re-locks a stale lockfile and a git source moves), by exact specifier (`uvx --from 'ocx-indexbot==0.2.0' indexbot`), or by naming no resolver at all (`indexbot`, a container entrypoint, a vendored install). The value is otherwise free-form shell — only a newline is banned, since it IS the command a step runs, not a value substituted into one. The pattern here cannot express the pinning rule; `indexbot ci` enforces it at render time and WF-08 audits the rendered tree.

setup.description: A step that installs whatever `run` needs — a `uses:` target on GitHub (typically a local composite action), an `image:` on GitLab. Empty renders no setup step at all. No newline — see `run`.

deploy_workflow.description: The workflow file a merged machine-lane PR should dispatch, if this deployment has one. Empty renders no such job at all. Renders unquoted into a shell command (`gh workflow run <deploy_workflow> --repo "$REPO" --ref main`) in a job holding `actions: write` + `contents: write`, so it takes a bare-filename grammar (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`) rather than just a newline ban — nothing a path component or a shell word boundary could hide in.

schedules.description: Cron expressions for the scheduled lanes. GitHub only: GitLab schedules are project settings rather than pipeline config.

reconcile.description: A 5-field cron expression (minute hour day month weekday). Shape-checked only, to keep it from breaking out of the quoted scalar it is rendered into.

stale.description: A 5-field cron expression (minute hour day month weekday). Shape-checked only, to keep it from breaking out of the quoted scalar it is rendered into.
